question.disease_name: Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

sampled_features.disease_name: Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

additional_requirements: delusions_and_hallucinations occur exclusively during the manic episode

S019.name: Delusions
S019.description: Fixed beliefs that do not change easily, even in the face of contradictory evidence.

subtypes.Persecutory Delusions: The false belief that one is being harmed or monitored by other people or organizations.
subtypes.Referential Delusions: The conviction that ordinary events, remarks, or behaviors have specific relevance to oneself.
subtypes.Grandiose Delusions: The false belief that one possesses special abilities, power, or fame.
subtypes.Erotomanic Delusions: The false belief that another person is in love with or has affection for them.
subtypes.Nihilistic Delusions: A destructive or negative conviction that the world is ending or that a major catastrophe will occur.
subtypes.Somatic Delusions: The baseless conviction that there is a serious abnormality with one's body or organs.
subtypes.Jealous Delusions: The conviction that one's spouse or romantic partner is being unfaithful without sufficient evidence.

S033.name: Elevated_Irritable_Mood
S033.description: A distinct period of abnormally and persistently elevated, expansive, or irritable mood.

subtypes.Elevated Mood: A mood that is abnormally high, euphoric, and full of unmotivated happiness and vitality.
subtypes.Irritable Mood: A state where one gets angry or aggressive even at minor stimuli.
subtypes.Mood Lability: Rapid shifts in mood, alternating unpredictably between euphoria and irritability.

S034.name: Increased_Activity
S034.description: Abnormally and persistently increased goal-directed activity or energy.

subtypes.Increased Energy: Overflowing physical and mental energy, leading to an inability to stay still and a desire to keep moving.
subtypes.Hyperactivity: Doing far more work than usual or starting multiple activities simultaneously.
subtypes.Psychomotor Agitation: Inability to tolerate resting or stopping, driven by a constant need to do something.

S035.name: Inflated_Self_Esteem
S035.description: Inflated self-esteem or grandiosity (may range from uncritical self-confidence to delusional proportions).

subtypes.Inflated Self-Confidence: Feeling capable of anything and believing that failure is impossible, unlike one's usual self.
subtypes.Overestimation of Abilities: Unrealistically assessing one's talents, knowledge, or abilities as superior.
subtypes.Grandiose Delusions: The false belief that one is a special and important person with a special mission or purpose.

S037.name: Pressured_Speech
S037.description: More talkative than usual or pressure to keep talking.

subtypes.Talkativeness: Speaking far more than usual and continuing to talk without rest.
subtypes.Rapid Speech: Speech speed is so fast that it is difficult for others to understand or interrupt.
subtypes.Pressured Speech: Cannot stop talking or tolerate silence due to an internal pressure to keep speaking.

S039.name: Manic_Distractibility
S039.description: Attention is too easily drawn to unimportant or irrelevant external stimuli.

subtypes.Responsiveness to Extraneous Stimuli: Attention is immediately drawn to trivial and unimportant stimuli nearby (e.g., noise, movement).
subtypes.Frequent Task Switching: Unable to finish one task and constantly shifting attention to new things, starting multiple tasks simultaneously.
subtypes.Inability to Sustain Attention: Unable to focus on any activity for long, with attention constantly being scattered.

S040.name: Increased_Goal_Activity
S040.description: Increase in goal-directed activity (at work, school, socially, or sexually) or purposeless psychomotor agitation.

subtypes.Occupational Hyperactivity: Driving significantly more projects or work than usual in the workplace or academic setting.
subtypes.Social Hyperactivity: Becoming much more sociable and extroverted than usual, actively meeting and contacting people.
subtypes.Hypersexuality: Significantly increased interest in or activity regarding sex.
subtypes.Psychomotor Agitation: Purposeless non-goal-directed activity, such as pacing or hand-wringing, driven by an inability to sit still.

S041.name: Painful_Consequence_Behavior
S041.description: Excessive involvement in activities that have a high potential for painful consequences.

subtypes.Unrestrained Buying Sprees: Spending excessive amounts of money or shopping recklessly to a degree that creates financial distress for self and family.
subtypes.Foolish Business Investments: Making rash business investments or ventures without sufficient review.
subtypes.Sexual Indiscretions: Engaging in indiscriminate or risky sexual behavior that is out of character.
subtypes.Impulsive Risky Behavior: Excessively dangerous or foolish behavior, such as reckless driving or drug use, without considering the consequences.

info.persona: Roberto Cordero is a 43‑year‑old methodical tech leader who channels curiosity, competitive drive, and a love for heritage traditions into art‑driven software, disciplined finance, health monitoring, solitary hikes, and vivid culinary experiments, all flavored by occasional impulsive tech splurges.
info.professional_persona: Roberto Cordero, a senior full‑stack developer, blends his methodical engineering mindset with a passion for generative visual experiences, and they lead small, focused teams to deliver scalable web platforms that double as interactive art installations while still keeping hands‑on code.
info.cultural_background: Roberto grew up in a bilingual Mexican‑American household, speaking both Spanish and English at home. Family gatherings centered around Sunday lunches featuring homemade tacos, rice, and beans, underscored by stories of his grandparents' migration from central Mexico. He celebrates Día de los Muertos and Mexican Independence Day with his extended family, often helping to set up altars and bake pan de muerto. His cultural identity informs his aesthetic sensibility—he frequently incorporates motifs from Mexican muralism and folk art into his digital creations. While fully integrated into the broader Glendale community, Roberto remains active in a local Mexican cultural association, volunteering at events that promote traditional music, dance, and cuisine. This dual cultural immersion nurtures a strong sense of pride in his heritage while fostering an openness to diverse artistic influences.
info.hobbies_and_interests: Outside of work, Roberto indulges in a mix of solitary and low‑key social activities that satisfy his curiosity and love for art. He creates digital paintings and generative art pieces using Processing and p5.js, often experimenting with algorithmic color palettes inspired by traditional Mexican folk art. He enjoys hiking the Sonoran Desert trails near Glendale, where the stark landscapes feed his reflective side. Cooking authentic Mexican dishes—especially mole and tamales—offers a creative culinary outlet and a way to stay connected with family traditions. He is an avid reader of science‑fiction and speculative nonfiction, a regular participant in local chess meet‑ups, and a frequent attendee of small gallery openings that showcase emerging artists. Occasionally, he joins community hackathons, where his competitive edge finds a constructive outlet.
info.sports_persona: Roberto Cordero, an avid weekend hiker, follows the Sonoran Desert Trail Club, frequently tackles the McDowell Mountains, cheers for the Los Angeles Lakers, and they join a local pickup basketball league when time permits, balancing solitary trail runs with occasional team sport camaraderie.
info.arts_persona: Roberto Cordero, a digital artist who creates generative pieces in Processing inspired by folk motifs, frequents LACMA and smaller gallery openings showcasing emerging talent, and they draw creative influence from James Turrell’s light installations, the murals of Diego Rivera, and Beeple’s NFT collections.
info.travel_persona: Roberto Cordero, a meticulous planner who maps weekend getaways in a spreadsheet, enjoys desert retreats in Sedona, cultural immersion trips to Oaxaca and historic tours of Kyoto, but they also indulge in spontaneous road trips along the Pacific Coast when a sudden break appears.
info.culinary_persona: Roberto Cordero, a seasoned home cook, masterfully prepares mole with dried chilies, chocolate, and spices, and they perfect tamales and pan de muerto for family gatherings, while occasionally over‑seasoning salsa when distracted by a new coding project.

info.persona: Dolores Galvagni balances the soothing rhythm of garden cycles and knitting needles with bouts of anxiety-driven overcommitment to freelance projects, often forgetting to file taxes on time while rewarding neighbors with hand-made scarves.
info.professional_persona: Dolores Galvagni, a 54-year-old scientific and technical illustrator, melds her engineering and mathematics background with artistic practice to produce precise hand-drawn and digital renderings for academic publishers, leverages Adobe Creative Suite, Blender, and AutoCAD in a freelance workflow that she structures around a comforting routine yet tolerates occasional schedule slips, mentors emerging artists through community workshops, teaches adjunct courses at a local college, and assertively pursues steady illustration contracts while flexibly balancing the unpredictable nature of freelance income.
info.cultural_background: Dolores grew up in a middle-class, white family in the greater Baltimore area, immersed in the Mid-Atlantic’s blend of suburban stability and proximity to the nation’s capital. Her upbringing emphasized practicality, self-reliance, and a respect for tradition—values reflected in her preference for routine and familiar surroundings. While her ethnic background is broadly Anglo-American, she has been shaped by Maryland’s diverse cultural offerings: the strong public school system that supported her STEM education, the vibrant arts scene along the Chesapeake Bay, and community events that celebrate local history. This mix of practical, suburban roots and exposure to artistic expression informs both her work ethic and creative sensibility.
info.hobbies_and_interests: In her downtime, Dolores finds comfort in routine activities that balance solitude with light social interaction. She tends a small vegetable garden behind her house, finding the predictable cycles of planting and harvest soothing. She enjoys knitting scarves and a few blanket projects, often gifting them to neighbors or art-group members. Regular hikes along the Patuxent River Trail provide a quiet escape, while the occasional visit to the Baltimore Museum of Art fuels her appreciation for both classic and contemporary works. She also reads historical fiction and attends local poetry readings, allowing her to stay connected to a creative community without overwhelming her schedule.
info.sports_persona: Dolores Galvagni hikes the Patuxent River Trail each spring and autumn as part of a local walking club, enjoys occasional yoga sessions at the community center, and roots for the Baltimore Ravens in football season and the Baltimore Orioles during summer baseball, preferring low-impact activities that complement her garden-filled lifestyle.
info.arts_persona: Dolores Galvagni frequents the Baltimore Museum of Art to study works by Georgia O'Keeffe, Mark Rothko, and Yayoi Kusama, channels Leonardo da Vinci's meticulous draftsmanship into her scientific illustrations, and participates in poetry readings where she admires spoken-word artists such as Sarah Kay and Rupi Kaur.
info.travel_persona: Dolores Galvagni prefers low-key weekend getaways to nearby historic towns like Annapolis and the Shenandoah Valley, plans trips meticulously using travel forums and recommendations from her craft network, yet dreams of a cultural immersion in the Scottish Highlands and a leisurely exploration of Florence's art districts when her retirement savings allow.
info.culinary_persona: Dolores Galvagni enjoys cooking farm-to-table meals such as roasted beet and carrot medleys seasoned with rosemary from her garden, hearty lentil stew with fresh thyme, and occasional chicken pot pie, displaying a competent but not professional skill level and relishes the crisp bite of heirloom tomatoes paired with aged cheddar.

info.persona: Allen Walker, a contemplative octogenarian artist, balances a lifelong love for solitary creative exploration with a whimsical penchant for impulsive art‑related splurges, all while navigating persistent anxiety through mindful routines and community connections.
info.professional_persona: Allen Walker, a 73‑year‑old self‑taught multidisciplinary artist, fuses abstract watercolor, improvisational piano, analog photography, and woodworking into community‑focused installations, channeling his spontaneous imagination and deep curiosity into a legacy‑building exhibition at the Schiller Park Community Center while mentoring local youth through informal art workshops.
info.cultural_background: Allen grew up in a working-class, white Catholic family in Schiller Park, a suburb with deep Polish, German and Irish roots. The neighborhood's modest, community-oriented ethos shaped his appreciation for small-group connections and local traditions. While his cultural upbringing emphasized modesty and practical skills, his curiosity led him to explore broader artistic currents in nearby Chicago, exposing him to the city's historic blues, jazz, and avant-garde art scenes. This blend of Midwestern pragmatism and urban artistic influence informs his creative outlook, valuing both the comfort of familiar community rituals and the excitement of novel, abstract expression.
info.hobbies_and_interests: Allen finds solace and stimulation in solitary walks through nearby forest preserves, where he sketches natural forms and contemplates abstract ideas. He collects and develops 35mm film, often experimenting with experimental darkroom techniques. He reads contemporary poetry, speculative fiction, and works of philosophy that challenge conventional thinking. He listens to avant-garde jazz and ambient soundscapes, occasionally attending small listening sessions at local cafés. He tends a modest vegetable garden, experimenting with heirloom varieties. He occasionally joins a close-knit circle of friends for weekly chess games and shared poetry readings. He also enjoys cooking inventive, spice-infused dishes that blend traditional Midwestern comfort food with global flavors.
info.sports_persona: Allen Walker, an avid follower of the Chicago Cubs and Chicago Bears, spends his mornings on the Schiller Park Senior Hiking Club’s walks through nearby forest preserves, joins the community’s seasonal co‑ed softball league in spring, and embraces winter ice‑skating sessions at the local rink to keep active, all while maintaining a gentle rivalry with his weekly chess group for strategic stamina.
info.arts_persona: Allen Walker, a passionate devotee of avant‑garde jazz legends Sun Ra and Ornette Coleman, experimental composer William Basinski, and visual painters Mark Rothko and Agnes Martin, regularly attends intimate listening sessions at a neighborhood café, curates small‑scale mixed‑media exhibitions featuring his own photographs and sculptures, and draws inspiration from the city’s historic blues clubs to infuse his works with a resonant, abstract narrative.
info.travel_persona: Allen Walker has trekked the Lake Michigan shoreline towns of Grand Haven and Saugatuck, soaked in New Orleans’ jazz ambience, explored the Ozark National Forest, and now dreams of a pilgrimage to the medieval monasteries of the Czech Republic and a serene retreat in Norway’s fjords, planning each journey with modest savings and a preference for off‑peak, contemplative travel.
info.culinary_persona: Allen Walker, a moderately skilled home chef, delights in reinventing classic Midwestern chicken pot pie with smoked paprika, rosemary, and a dash of harissa, pairs it with heirloom tomato‑basil gazpacho, and experiments with kimchi‑fried rice flavored by gochujang and locally sourced corn, often sourcing fresh produce from his own vegetable garden and savoring the process as a sensory extension of his artistic practice.
